newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power steady despite tighter supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power steady despite tighter supply.

text.p: Western U.S. spot power prices were steady Friday ahead of typically thin weekend demand, but held on to gains made Thursday when the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) withdrew from the spot market, traders said.
"We saw some short-covering in the futures market early today, but it didn't really spill over into cash," said one trader.
BPA stayed out of the spot market again for Saturday and Sunday, but offered 300 megawatts for Monday preschedulings.
The federal agency offered non-firm power during peak demand hours on Monday at $20.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) in the Northwest and at $22.00 at the California-Oregon border (COB).
Traders reported Monday firm, peak deals at COB near $21.00, compared with quotes at $21.00-22.00 on Thursday.
Off-peak quotes at COB were seen at $17.00-18.00, up from $16.00-17.00.
Monday Mid-Columbia prices were also seen near $21.00, unchanged from Thursday.
Firm, peak power at Palo Verde for Monday was last quoted $19.25-20.00 per MWh, compared with $19.00-20.00 on Thursday.
